Petitioner who is arraigned as accused No.1 has filed this petition under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C.) with a prayer to quash the criminal proceeding initiated against him in C.C.No.1686/2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 of IPC on the file of III Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Hubballi.
2. In support of the petition, the petitioner has contended that he is innocent and law abiding citizen and has not committed the offence.
He has been falsely implicated based on the complaint filed by his wife Asifa Kousar.
The trial court has wrongly taken cognizance and issued summons to him.
There is no material to attract the required ingredients to file the case against the petitioner.

Continuation of the proceedings would amount to abuse of the process of the court and pray to allow the petition.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:16174 3.

Learned HCGP representing respondent No.1- State and learned counsel representing respondent No.2/ complainant submitted oral objections stating that the marriage of petitioner and complainant was performed on 27.10.2002.
On the demand made by the petitioner and his family members, gold weighing 10 tolas, Hero Honda motorcycle and household articles worth Rs.2,00,000/- were given.
After the marriage, petitioner and complainant lived together at Bengaluru.

Sister of the petitioner and his family members who are arraigned as accused Nos.2 to 11 used to abuse and harass the complainant saying that she is a barren woman and not able to bear children and therefore, petitioner should contract a second marriage.
Being instigated by accused Nos.2 to 11, petitioner used to abuse and assault her.
He used to tell that she is not good looking and has not brought sufficient dowry.
3.1 On the complaint made by the complainant, the Whitefield Police summoned and advised the petitioner.
Even accused Nos.7 and 8 who are residing at Germany NC: 2024:KHC-D:16174 used to harass and ill-treat her when they visited India and instigated petitioner to contract second marriage.
On 25.08.2021, complainant came to know that petitioner has contracted second marriage.
On 15.09.2021 at 11.00 a.m., when complainant and her family members visited the house of the petitioner, accused Nos.2 to 11 abused and assaulted her.

sentences.text: Based on the complaint, the jurisdictional police registered the case and taken up investigation and filed charge sheet against the petitioner.
The police have not filed charge sheet against accused Nos.2 to 11.
There is prima facie material to proceed against the petitioner.
The allegations made against the petitioner are required to be proved at the trial.
This is not a fit case for quashing the proceedings and pray to dismiss the petition.

4. Heard arguments and perused the record.
5.
Complainant is wife of the petitioner.
Their marriage took place on 27.10.2002.

There is specific NC: 2024:KHC-D:16174 allegation that at the time of marriage, petitioner and other accused demanded and received dowry in the form of gold weighing 10 tolas, Hero Honda motorcycle and household articles worth Rs.2,00,000/-.
After the marriage, petitioner and complainant set up separate residence at Bengaluru.
It appears, the complainant did not beget children and accused Nos.2 to 11 being his family members were instigating the petitioner to contract a second marriage.
Ultimately the petitioner succeeded in contracting second marriage on 25.08.2021.
When the complainant and her family members questioned the petitioner and his family members about the same, they were abused and assaulted.
6. After conducting detailed investigation, the concerned police filed charge sheet only against the petitioner.
Of course, at the trial, if the trial court finds that there is also evidence against other accused, it may proceed against them under section 319 of Cr.P.C.
At this stage, there is sufficient material to proceed against the NC: 2024:KHC-D:16174 petitioner.
In the light of the substantive allegations and supporting evidence collected at the investigation, this is not a fit case for quashing the criminal proceedings against the petitioner/accused No.1.
The prosecution is required to be provided with opportunity to prove the allegations made against the petitioner.

7. In the result, the petition fails and accordingly, the following;
ORDER i) Petition filed by the petitioner/accused No.1 under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is dismissed.
ii) Send a copy of the order to the trial court forthwith.
